source.title: ANCRe: Adaptive Neural Connection Reassignment for Efficient Depth Scaling
source.authors: Yilang Zhang; Bing-Cong Li; Niao He; G. B. Giannakis

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, appendices, and checklist; no truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results on how residual topology and learned connection reassignment affect optimization, including gradient-flow convergence on deep linear networks and training outcomes in larger models. These bear on V3's depth and shortcut component, but it does not measure CIFAR classification training error.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own gradient-flow loss results for deep linear networks and empirical results that compare ANCRe with cascaded residual connections. The comparisons of ANCRe's granularity and auxiliary metrics are included only where they report the tested topology intervention's outcome. Cited prior studies on normalization and initialization are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual connections as an architectural tool and evaluates residual topology and ANCRe. Its linear-regression convergence results concern linear networks, whereas V3 names depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional classifiers and its prevention by identity shortcuts. Modern-model experiments compare residual architectures using validation perplexity, generation metrics or RL performance. None tests V1–V6 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that residual topology affects convergence and that ANCRe improves performance and depth efficiency across their tested settings. Their theoretical analysis is restricted to linear networks. Reduced effectiveness in architectures with optimized topology or less reusable intermediate representations is proposed as a potential limitation, rather than demonstrated by controlled results.
record.recipe_differences: The paper changes residual topology by learning weighted shortcut coefficients (ANCRe), and analyzes linear-network gradient flow; it does not use the original CIFAR classification recipes or measure classification training error. Its empirical comparisons train foundation and RL models against conventional residual connections.
record.method_sensitivity: Residual connection placement and normalization scheme alter convergence or reported performance; for LLaMA, unnormalized ANCRe diverges, ingoing normalization has lower perplexity than outgoing normalization, and topology ablations produce different outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear-network convergence slows with depth; cascaded shortcuts accelerate convergence, and shortcut placement changes convergence rates. The slow-case theorem is existential; the fast-case bound holds under sufficiently small initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual topology can change squared-loss convergence from polynomial to exponential decay in deep linear networks under the specified gradient-flow assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: ANCRe improves validation perplexity over cascaded residual connections across the eight LLaMA size and optimizer combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned residual routing improves validation perplexity and convergence efficiency in the tested LLaMA pre-training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: ANCRe improves FID for both tested DiT sizes with and without classifier-free guidance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned residual routing improves image-generation metrics in the tested DiT pre-training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report faster time-at-goal convergence across four RL tasks; a 16-layer ANCRe ResNet can match or surpass a 64-layer conventional ResNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned residual routing improves goal-reaching performance and depth efficiency in the tested RL networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Unnormalized ANCRe diverges, ingoing normalization outperforms outgoing normalization, and topology ablations perform worse or diverge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ANCRe stability and perplexity depend on routing-coefficient normalization and topology design.

fits_no_version.finding: A fixed first-and-previous-layer topology performs worse than ANCRe, while frozen learned routing coefficients retain nearly all gains on retraining.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned routing coefficients encode a transferable topology advantage in the tested LLaMA models.

record.problems: The central theoretical convergence analysis is limited to deep linear networks, with whitened inputs and gradient flow; extension to nonlinear networks is left for future work. Modern-model results mainly use validation perplexity, FID, or RL time-at-goal rather than training classification error. Many plotted results are figure-only, and the text does not provide per-condition values or uncertainty; multi-seed mean and SD are reported only for 60M, 130M, and 350M FullPT LLaMA runs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap. Figure-only RL conditions are retained separately because task and depth are separately reported in Figure 8 and the text states the aggregate result across all four tasks.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training-error interpolation, including random labels, model size and training-recipe conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and its dependence on extra student neurons.

Depth-dependent training classification error in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut counterparts; longer training; deep plain tanh initialization and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine with respect to the supplied claim versions; this does not negate the reported ANCRe improvements. Related linear-network results do not justify extending V3 beyond the systems and behavior it names. No verdict labels apply, and no omitted results directly test a supplied version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification training error, random or corrupted labels, model size thresholds, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and student width relative to teacher width.

The paper tests the depth and residual-topology convergence question in linear networks and reports modern residual-network training outcomes, but it does not compare plain versus identity-shortcut networks on classification training error. Its ResNet RL experiment uses a learned reassignment method and reports goal-reaching performance, not training classification error.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth in plain tanh or convolutional networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, loss-curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence at different rates.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup as a normalization-free comparison.
